properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 3:38PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 337 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 11
miles south of Lake City, or 50 miles southwest of Gunnison, moving
northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of central Hinsdale
County.

This includes Colorado 149 between mile markers 47 and 60.
properties.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 3:33PM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
At 333 PM MDT/433 PM CDT/, Doppler radar was tracking a cluster of
strong thunderstorms 4 miles northeast of Bonny Reservoir. These
storms were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 55 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of southeastern Yuma
County in northeastern Colorado, northeastern Kit Carson County in
east central Colorado, western Cheyenne and northwestern Sherman
Counties in northwestern Kansas, including the following locations...
Hale, Idalia, and Beecher Island.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 70 in Colorado between mile markers 445 and 447.
Highway 385 between mile markers 201 and 229.
properties.areaDesc: Yuma County; Kit Carson County; Cheyenne; Sherman

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 27 at 3:32PM MDT until July 27 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
SVRGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
South central Garfield County in west central Colorado...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 332 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 15 miles northwest
of De Beque, or 32 miles north of Grand Junction, moving east at 10
mph.

HAZARD...Half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

* This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
south central Garfield County.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 27 at 3:30PM MDT until July 27 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Garfield County in west central Colorado...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 330 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain above Roan Creek. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of creeks and streams, county roads.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of South Central Garfield County along Roan
Creek

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 3:24PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 324 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a cluster of strong
thunderstorms 19 miles northwest of Parachute, or 36 miles north of
Grand Junction, moving east at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation and
outdoor objects is possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of south central
Garfield County.
properties.areaDesc: Central Yampa River Basin; Roan and Tavaputs Plateaus; Debeque to Silt Corridor

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 27 at 2:41PM MDT until July 27 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
East Central Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
Southwestern Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 545 PM MDT.

* At 241 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. The expected
rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to
Beulah.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 1:36PM MDT until July 27 at 4:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar
is possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter and Cutler Creek drainages and Highway 550.

* WHEN...Until 445 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and
other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 133 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Gunnison, CO; Hinsdale, CO; Ouray, CO

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 12:38PM MDT until July 27 at 3:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of west central Colorado, including the following
counties, Mesa and Montrose and Utah, including the following
counties, Grand and San Juan.

* WHEN...Until 345 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1238 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.4 and 0.8 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
mainly rural areas of Southwestern Mesa, Western Montrose,
Southeastern Grand and Northeastern San Juan Counties
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Mesa, CO; Montrose, CO; Grand, UT; San Juan, UT
